Rose Raspberry Macarons for Gaudete Sunday

Served at: Gaudete Sunday

Makes 24-30 assembled macaronsPrep 45 min (plus 1-2 hours resting time)Cook 12-15 min per batch

Gaudete Sunday, the third Sunday of Advent, is a joyful pause in the solemn Advent season, marked by the lighting of the pink candle and rose-colored vestments. These delicate Rose Raspberry Macarons, with their festive pink hue and sweet filling, offer a perfect way to celebrate this day of rejoicing with a special, homemade treat.

Ingredients

  • For the Macaron Shells:
  • 100 g (1 cup) almond flour, finely ground
  • 100 g (1 cup) powdered sugar
  • 70 g (about 2 large) egg whites, aged at room temperature for a few hours or overnight
  • 100 g (1/2 cup) granulated sugar
  • Pinch of salt (optional)
  • 2-3 drops pink gel food coloring
  • For the Raspberry Buttercream Filling:
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 cups (240 g) powdered sugar
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1-2 tablespoons milk or cream
  • 1/4 cup (60 g) good quality raspberry jam

Method

  1. Prepare two baking sheets by lining them with parchment paper or silicone mats. If desired, draw 1.5-inch (4 cm) circles on the parchment paper, spaced about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart.
  2. In a medium bowl, sift together the almond flour and powdered sugar. Discard any large pieces of almond that don't pass through the sieve. Sift again into a clean bowl to ensure a very fine mixture.
  3. In a separate large, clean bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt on medium speed until foamy. Gradually add the granulated sugar, one tablespoon at a time, continuing to beat on high speed until the meringue is glossy and forms stiff peaks. Add the pink gel food coloring and beat until fully incorporated.
  4. Add about one-third of the dry ingredients to the meringue. Using a rubber spatula, gently fold them in. Add the remaining dry ingredients in two more additions, folding until just combined. Continue to fold, scraping down the sides of the bowl, until the batter flows like lava from your spatula and forms a 'figure eight' when dropped back into the bowl (this is called 'macaronage'). Be careful not to overmix.
  5. Transfer the macaron batter to a piping bag fitted with a round tip (e.g., Wilton 1A or Ateco 806).
  6. Pipe uniform circles onto the prepared baking sheets, following your drawn guides if using. Hold the piping bag straight up and pipe from the center, lifting straight up when done.
  7. Firmly tap the baking sheets on the counter 2-3 times to release any trapped air bubbles. Use a toothpick to pop any remaining bubbles on the surface of the shells.
  8. Let the piped macarons rest at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours, or until a skin forms on top and they are no longer sticky to the touch. This step is crucial for developing the 'feet'.
  9. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C) during the last 30 minutes of the resting period.
  10. Bake one tray at a time for 12-15 minutes, or until the 'feet' have formed and the shells are firm and don't wobble when gently touched. If they brown too quickly, you can slightly reduce the oven temperature.
  11. Carefully remove the baking sheets from the oven and let the macaron shells cool completely on the sheets before attempting to peel them off. This prevents breakage.
  12. While the shells cool, prepare the filling: In a medium bowl, beat the softened butter with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Gradually add the powdered sugar, beating until smooth. Beat in the vanilla extract and 1 tablespoon of milk or cream. Add more milk/cream if needed to reach a spreadable consistency. Fold in the raspberry jam until just combined.
  13. Once the macaron shells are completely cool, match them up by size. Pipe or spread a dollop of raspberry buttercream onto the flat side of one shell, then gently top with a matching shell to create a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining shells.
  14. Store the assembled macarons in an airtight container in the refrigerator for at least 24 hours before serving for the best flavor and texture. Let them come to room temperature for about 15-20 minutes before enjoying.

Tips

  • Aged egg whites (separated a day or two in advance and left in a covered container at room temperature) whip up better and create a more stable meringue.
  • Do not overmix the macaron batter during the 'macaronage' stage; it should flow slowly, not run. Overmixing leads to flat macarons without 'feet'.
  • Oven temperature can vary significantly. It's recommended to use an oven thermometer to ensure accuracy, as consistent heat is key for macaron success.
